findings.decompiled: _28 = sha3(mem[_26 + 32 len mem[_26]]) ... signer3 = ecrecover(sha3(mem[mem[64] + 32 len _25 - mem[64] + 290]), v, r, s); mem[_25 + 322 len min(32, return_data.size)] = ext_call.return_data[...]; _35 = mem[_25 + 334 len 20] and mem[_25 + 334 len 20] == owner; allowance[concat(Bytes(12, 0), mem[_25 + 334 len 20])][spender] = value
findings.source: solmate ERC20.sol:130-156 ecrecover(keccak256(abi.encodePacked("\x19\x01", DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(), keccak256(abi.encode(PERMIT_TYPEHASH, owner, spender, value, nonces[owner]++, deadline)))), v, r, s); require(recovered != 0 && recovered == owner); allowance[recovered][spender] = value
findings.issue: Because mem[64] is 128 or 320 depending on the chainid branch, the struct hash and the EIP-712 digest stay raw memory slices; the named result `signer3` is never used and the signer is re-read as `mem[_25 + 334 len 20]`, also as the allowance key. The lines are exact (mem[64] = _25 + 224, length 66) but the digest and the signer are unreadable.
findings.rule: Resolve buffers relative to a symbolic base (b = mem[64] at the join) so sha3(mem[b + 32 len mem[b]]) with mem[b] = 192 becomes sha3(w1..w6) and the packed one sha3(Bytes(2, 0x1901), _22, _28). The word at the output of a STATICCALL to address 1 whose output word was zeroed before and not written since equals the recovered address (0 on empty return); substitute the named result for it.

findings.function: convertToShares, convertToAssets, preview*, maxWithdraw, deposit, mint, withdraw, redeem (FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown/Up)
findings.source: FixedPointMathLib.sol:44 if iszero(mul(denominator, iszero(mul(y, gt(x, div(MAX_UINT256, y)))))) { revert(0, 0) }
findings.issue: The overflow/zero-denominator check is a product of booleans and values, which reads as arithmetic; it means totalSupply != 0 and not (totalAssets != 0 and shares > max / totalAssets).
findings.rule: When a product is used only as a truth value and one factor is known to be 0 or 1, `b * x` equals `b and x` (no wrap is possible), so print the condition with and/or (here `require totalSupply and (not totalAssets or shares <= -1 / totalAssets)`).

findings.decompiled: if not uint1(name): mem[128] = 256 * name.field_8; _5 = _1 * bool(_1) + 128 else: mem[128 len ceil32(_1)] = stor[sha3(0) len (_1 + 31) / 32]; _5 = _1 + 128 ... sha3(mem[128 len _5 - 128])
findings.issue: keccak256(bytes(name)) is shown as the two-armed short/long copy of the storage string and a hash of the slice; `_1 * bool(_1)` is just `_1`.
findings.rule: `x * bool(x) == x` for every x. When both arms of the storage byte-array decode write the array's bytes at mem[p len length], merge them into one copy line `mem[p len length] = name[all]`, so the hash prints as sha3(name[all]).

findings.decompiled: def withdraw(uint256 shares, address to, address from): ... totalAssets = SafeMath.sub(totalAssets, shares) ... log Withdraw(..., assets=shares, shares=_3); call 0x0.transfer(to, shares)
findings.source: solmate ERC4626.sol withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)
findings.issue: The signature database's parameter names call the asset amount `shares`, so the text reads as if shares were subtracted from totalAssets and sent out, while _3 (the real shares) is burned.
findings.rule: When the parameter names of a signature entry conflict with the named event fields the parameters are emitted as (here Withdraw.assets), prefer the event's names or neutral _paramN names.

notes: Solmate ERC4626 + ERC20 (pack had no source definitions; sources read in lib/solmate/src). No source loops; name()/symbol() return copies and the name hash copy are copy lines. All conditions, events, storage writes and SafeTransferLib checks match. deposit/mint read the success check as ext_call.return_data[0] while withdraw/redeem keep the partial copy into mem[0] (after mem[0] = owner/from); both are exact because the `return_data.size <= 31` disjunct makes the word irrelevant when it is short. P8: scratch writes for hashes printed with values (343, 347-352, 355-356). The Deposit event is printed with another contract's field names (token, user, amount, balance) from the database.
summary: Faithful text of a solmate ERC4626 vault; immutables read as 0 (artifact). The main readability problem is permit, whose digest and recovered signer stay raw memory relative to the free-memory pointer.
